title: Sprint Symphony: Release-Train Traffic Controller for Multi-Surface Launches
creator: Ava Kline
description: Problem: Launches across runtime, console, and API surfaces frequently collide on capacity and stakeholder availability, resulting in last-minute throttles, rollback risk, and manual firefighting. Goal: Deliver a lightweight orchestration service and playbook termed 'Traffic Controller' that schedules release slots, scores conflicting requests, provides automated capacity guardrails, and surfaces clear owner-level runbooks and rehearsal checklists. The scope covers calendar data model, slot scoring algorithm, advisor signals for Dedicated reservations, console integrations for visual lanes, and an ops runbook for week-of-launch behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Calendar schema supports named lanes (eg. fast-lane, regional, maintenance) and slot metadata (owner, surface, capacity-commit, blackout windows)
Automated conflict detection flags >20% capacity overlap and surfaces remediation suggestions in the console UI
Slot scoring algorithm implemented and documented (priority weightings for customer-impact, release-criticality, capacity-reserve) and validated against historical launches
Integrations: export to capacity-forecasting service and create tentative Dedicated reservations via API call
Launch runbook template and two rehearsals completed with stakeholders (runtime, console, API) and checklist stored in Drive
tasks: Draft data model and slot lifecycle (Ava)
Prototype scoring algorithm with historical launch data (Miguel, Data Science)
UI mockups for calendar lanes and conflict resolution (Design)
Backend scheduler service MVP and API endpoints (ENG)
Console integration to surface flags and owner actions (Console Team)
Capacity connector to Dedicated reservations and forecasting (Infra)
notes: 2026-03-10: Scoping meeting — agreed to prioritize lightweight automation over heavy gating to reduce operational friction. Decided on three lane types: critical, standard, and maintenance.

2026-03-11: Trade-off discussion — strict reservations reduce conflict but increase unused capacity; we will implement soft quotas with suggested reservation promotion if utilization exceeds threshold.
2026-03-11: Prototype spreadsheet exists (Drive link: https://drive.google.com/example/sprint-symphony-proto) showing slot scoring with sample weights.
2026-03-12: Design review scheduled; asked Priya Nair (Eng lead) and Kira Zhou (Design) for feedback on mockups. Mockups in Figma: https://figma.com/file/sprint-symphony-mockups
2026-03-12: Engineering flagged dependency on capacity telemetry (ENG-1842) and on console routing PR (ENG-4789).
Decisions: use event-based slot updates (webhooks) for cross-team notifications; keep initial UI read-only for non-owners to avoid edit conflicts.
Open risks: holiday blackout windows in EU region may concentrate launches in adjacent weeks — need capacity buffer heuristic.
Follow-ups: schedule cross-team rehearsal week-of-2026-03-22; allocate 2h working session to tune scoring weights with SRE and Sales Ops.
Artifacts: PRD draft: https://confluence.company.internal/Launch-Symphony-PRD (requested review from Product Docs), GitHub placeholder PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-train/pull/142
